questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Stop until the dog loses interest.
Ride alongside the dog.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, apply light pressure to the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What must a motorcycle's headlight do?

options.text: Be used only at night.
Be on at all times.
Be visible for at least 25 feet.
Be used only in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times when riding. This helps other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something your riding clothes should protect you from?

options.text: Sunburn
Windburn
Chapped lips
Dehydration

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. They should also provide extra protection in a crash.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgater may be focused on you and miss upcoming hazards that require slower traffic.

questions.question: How is maximum straight-line braking done?

options.text: Use the front brake, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel for maximum straight-line braking.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Follow me
Slow down
Speed up
Exit

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The drinker's body weight
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. It is illegal and dangerous to drive a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In areas with potential hazards, like school or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Slow down before you hit it.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you hit it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, slow down as much as possible before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel just before hitting the object.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Behind the operator.
The child does not need to reach the footrests.
The child should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child passenger should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may have trouble balancing and could interfere with the operator's control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's stopping distance?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in nearly the same distance. However, on wet or slippery pavement, motorcycles have a much harder time stopping quickly.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of the rounded mirrors on most motorcycles?

options.text: They are difficult to adjust to at first.
They make cars look closer than they are.
They show a narrow view of the road.
They make cars look farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars look farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Rounded mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances in these mirrors until you get used to them.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing your motorcycle?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Ride alongside the dog.
Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it at a low speed. Then speed up and leave it behind. For larger animals, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect blood alcohol content: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Move your shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and applying the brakes if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road hazards or conditions ahead.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when it is warm outside while riding?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and protects you at all times. Modern jackets are made to protect riders from overheating, even in warm weather.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve as separate actions, not at the same time. You can brake first and then swerve, or swerve first and then brake.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. In poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking and moving unnecessarily so you can focus on riding. Passengers should board only after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.
